newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. Mideast envoy going home - Israel Radio.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy going home - Israel Radio.

text.p: U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross has told Israel he will leave the Middle East, having failed to break a stalemate in Israeli-PLO talks after 15 days of trying, Israel Radio said on Monday.

It said he had told leaders he would go home and return to the region when the sides needed his help to hammer out an agreement on the deadlock over the long-delayed partial Israeli troop pullback from the West Bank city of Hebron.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office, where Ross and Netanyahu were meeting, had no immediate comment. Ross, sent to the region by U.S. President Bill Clinton, was due to hold a news conference shortly.

Israel and the PLO are trying to clinch a deal to implement a long-promised partial Israeli troop pullback from Hebron, the last and most sensitive of seven West Bank cities due to be handed over to Palestinian rule in a 1995 peace accord.

An outbreak of West Bank and Gaza violence that claimed the lives of 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis prompted Clinton to call a White House summit attended by Netanyahu and Arafat and send Ross to the region.
A PLO official said Washington would continue to be represented in the talks by U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk and U.S. Consul General in East Jerusalem Edward Abington.
A diplomatic source who declined to be identified said Ross might want to leave early to avoid devaluing his influence by continuing to participate in slow-moving negotiations.
